One of my biggest takeaways from Microsoft Ignite is the value of staying the course.
  
A year ago at Microsoft Ignite, we talked about Human Ambition, Intelligence and Trust, and introduced the foundations of what would become Microsoft IQ.
  
This year, we returned to those same ideas with much deeper product truth behind them. Microsoft IQ is now here, and enterprise customers are showing how they are putting it to work in their own Frontier transformations.
  
My conversations with customers this week reinforced why that progression matters. In a market moving this quickly, customers value consistency: a durable point of view, a continuously improving product portfolio and the ability to turn that innovation into meaningful outcomes for their organizations.
  
That kind of trust is something we have to keep earning. It means staying close to customers and the market, listening to what is working, where they need help and what we can learn from them.

Since September, I've been working with my Autopilot, Apollo, every day. 

It's become part of how I work – picking up long-running tasks and keeping them moving between meetings, overnight, and across milestones. Autopilot has been the first proactive and collaborative AI experience for me.  

For example, as I prepared for my Ignite travel and meetings, Apollo helped me with relevant background for press interviews and warned me about travel issues (I had a car to the wrong airport, before I had been rescheduled due to the ATC issues!). 

Today, Autopilot starts rolling out to Frontier customers. It can take on sustained work, keep it moving over time, and join Teams conversations just like another teammate.

This is a different way of working with AI. You don't just ask a question and get an answer. You hand off the work and it keeps going.

While Bing is our web search engine for humans, Web IQ is our search engine for AI agents. Web IQ provides web grounding to many companies and leading AI platforms like ChatGPT, Copilot, and Mistral.

At Microsoft Ignite, we’re announcing that Web IQ is now broadly available to all Azure customers. We’re also introducing new features and enhancements to help developers build more capable, enterprise-ready AI agents:

• Web IQ Auto and Auto Advanced leverage query fan outs and intelligent orchestration to help agents tackle complex questions and retrieve the evidence they need more efficiently.

• Scopes gives organizations greater control over the sources their agents use, making it easier to ground responses in preferred content. It is essentially custom search for agents.

• Expanded knowledge domains across places, weather, health, and commerce give agents richer, more relevant information to understand and act on what’s happening in the world.

Web grounding services generally optimize for quality, or speed, or token cost. What I’m most proud of is our team’s work to have Web IQ deliver industry-leading frontier performance on all 3 dimensions. This is in part thanks to our 20+ years of innovations in Bing, now re-designed for agents.

The blog below shares more details and includes benchmark results and outcomes from a variety of customers like Genspark, Publicis Groupe, and National Grid, which did their own comp evals and selected Web IQ given its benefits.

Congrats to the team. I’m excited to see what developers build next.

Our ambition with everything we are announcing at Ignite today is to parlay technological advances into real outcomes and new points of leverage for people, organizations, and society at large.

Just a few of the things we’re announcing:
Copilot Workspaces.
The time has come to move beyond single-player AI to a world where people and their agents work together, with shared context, towards a common goal. That's Copilot Workspaces.
New models.
For us, it's about mapping intelligence to a given task, with the best economics. This is something we can uniquely do in the context of real-world tasks by tuning our products, harness, tools, and the model system end to end.
 
Today, we're announcing Microsoft-Decision 1.1 (now GA), Code 2 (at the cost-performance frontier for enterprise coding), and Cyber 2 Flash (outperforming frontier models on security tasks at a fraction of the cost). 

And, of course, we have all the most popular closed and open weight models in Foundry too. We are very excited to bring
OpenAI
's GPT-6.2 to Foundry.
 
And we are announcing that
Meta
's latest models are all coming to Foundry, as well!
Agent 365 Business Analytics.
You can think of this as your ERP system for AI, helping organizations connect spend to business value and continuously optimize their return on intelligence.
Microsoft Perception.
Now GA, it brings together teams of red, blue, and green agents to deliver security outcomes at machine speed, with you always in control.
Microsoft AI Transparency Initiative.
We're working with 40+ organizations to establish open standards for AI that is accountable, independently verifiable, and safe by design.
HorizonDB.
Our distributed PostgreSQL database is now GA in Azure, delivering up to 8X the performance of self-managed Postgres.
 
And by bringing HorizonDB into Fabric, agents will be able to reason over live transactions alongside petabytes of historical data in real time.

Finally, we are also rearchitecting the core compute, storage, and networking primitives in Azure to execute, connect, and share context at agent scale.

It’s great to be at Microsoft Ignite, spending time with commercial customers and IT leaders.
 
Businesses run on Windows. That’s a privilege and a responsibility. It’s why we’re building Windows to be the trusted foundation for work and moving faster than ever on security.
 
A few of the updates we shared today:

The Windows endpoint security platform is now generally available.
